notes_for_editor: Core chronology rests on the NRHP nomination, which itself relies on NARA files. Disagreements flagged in text: 1838 vs 1839; pier 48 ft vs 45 ft (same nomination); distance to shore; Kate Walker's age at retirement (nomination 73; Noble birth year 1848 gives about 70); 1890 vs 1894/95 start (USLHS lists her from 1890; nomination says acting from June 1894). The 1903 and 1918 newspaper features name her husband Jacob; the nomination, USLHS and NPS say John. Niblett initial: S. in Bulletin, K. in USLHS. Raymond A. Shaffer's start year is a placeholder (archive gives '-1928'); John H. Monahan similar. Bulletin 1930 p.27 and 1921 p.32 are two-column OCR; quotes are short fragments matched by line. Date of Niblett rescue is only 'recently' in the 1921 volume. Newspaper accounts from 1903 and 1918 are features told in Kate's words, not logs. No photos added. Corpus holds Lighthouse Board reports only for 1891-1901 so 1883 events rely on the nomination. Fact-check 2026-10-22: Foundation site (2010 de-accessioned, Noble bought for $1, Foundation 2021) and Noble page (2009 surplus, 2011 award) disagree; both now stated. Bulletin page numbers confirmed with corpus.py page (1921 pp. 32, 48; 1930 p. 27). Roster excludes post-1960 USCG crew by design (living-people rule).
